reshared_post.reshared_text:
What is your take on it?

The book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies by Eliezer Yudkowsky and Nate Soares argues that creating a superhuman AI would inevitably cause human extinction.

Its core thesis is that because modern AIs are opaque, "grown" systems, their intelligence would be separate from human values. A superintelligent AI would pursue its own goals, which would inevitably conflict with human survival, not out of malice, but simply because humanity would be in the way.

The authors conclude that incremental safety is futile and advocate for a global, verifiable halt to powerful AI development to prevent this almost certain outcome. The book has been a controversial bestseller, praised as a vital warning by some and criticized as alarmist by others.
